page: OVHcloud rtx5000-56 is a GPU-accelerated server instance within the Cloud GPU family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor with 8 dedicated physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The x86_64 CPU architecture includes AVX, AVX512F, and AVX512_VNNI instruction set extensions. This compute foundation is paired with 56.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per core, and a local storage configuration of 400 GB SSD.

The primary hardware differentiator is the inclusion of two NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs from the Turing architecture family, delivering a combined total of 32 GB of VRAM. This hardware profile is supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong memory performance with a Passmark memory score in the top 25% and a small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth of 726.2 GB/sec. However, large-block memory write speeds are relatively weak at 19.55 GB/sec.

The dual-GPU configuration excels at machine learning tasks, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference benchmarks. For a small 135M model, it processes prompts at 9506.12 tokens per second and generates text at 387.2 tokens per second. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing reaches 1841.54 tokens per second with text generation at 67.32 tokens per second. In contrast, CPU-bound tasks like single-threaded gzip compression show weaker performance, while general database operations and static web serving remain in the average tier. This server is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring parallel GPU processing, such as LLM inference, rendering, and data science, rather than pure CPU-bound sequential processing.
